title: Interhemispheric monsoon dynamics over the past 450,000 years
title_zh: 过去45万年两个半球季风的动力学
abstract: The global monsoon system provides freshwater to much of Earth’s biota, including its human population1. The Milankovitch theory predicts changes in Earth’s solar insolation over geologic time, and these variations are expected to result in changes to the global monsoon2. Internal climate forcings, such as ice cover and sea surface temperatures, may also affect the system. However, few records of monsoon variability in the Southern Hemisphere over glacial–interglacial cycles exist to test our understanding of the factors that drive variations in the global monsoon. Here we show that monsoons in both the Southern and Northern Hemispheres vary with Milankovitch forcing, and with internal boundary conditions over the past 450,000 years. We present a record of South American Summer Monsoon (SASM) variability, based on speleothem oxygen-isotope data from the Amazon Basin. South American Summer Monsoon variability and that of a major Northern Hemisphere monsoon—that is, the Asian monsoon3,4—have been strikingly out of phase. However, we observe occasional synchronous behaviour in regions impacted by both monsoons. We identify a synchronicity threshold that is exceeded during ten events, including during glacial terminations. Comparison with palaeoclimatic forcing factors during these intervals indicates that greenhouse gas concentrations, cross-equatorial thermal gradients and sea surface temperatures in both the Atlantic and Pacific probably influence these events. This record demonstrates that the global monsoon can reorganize itself, especially during intervals of rapidly changing planetary boundary conditions. A 450 ka Andean speleothem record shows Southern and Northern Hemisphere monsoons generally vary out of phase, but occasionally synchronize during rapid climate change and glacial terminations.
abstract_zh: 全球季风系统为地球生物圈（包括人类）提供淡水。Milankovitch理论预测地球在地质年代内的太阳辐射变化，并预期这些变化将导致全球季风的变化。内部气候强迫因素，如冰盖和海面温度，也可能影响该系统。然而，缺乏来自南半球在冰期-间冰期循环中的季风变化记录，以检验我们对驱动全球季风变化因素的理解。在此，我们表明，在过去45万年中，南北半球季风都随Milankovitch强迫和内部边界条件而变化。我们基于亚马逊盆地钟乳石氧同位素数据，呈现了南美夏季季风（SASM）的变化记录。南美夏季季风的变化与主要北半球季风——即亚洲季风——的变化表现出显著的不同相位。然而，我们观察到在同时受两个季风影响的地区出现偶尔的同步行为。我们确定了一个同步阈值，该阈值在十个事件中被超过，包括在冰期结束期间。与这些间隔的古气候强迫因素比较表明，温室气体浓度、跨赤道热量梯度以及大西洋和太平洋的海面温度可能影响了这些事件。这项记录表明，全球季风可以在行星边界条件快速变化的间隔期间重新组织自身。一份45万年的安第斯钟乳石记录显示，南北半球季风通常呈不同相位变化，但在快速气候变化和冰期结束期间偶尔同步。
